content.title: How to watch the Masters today, Round 3 start time, TV schedule
content.text: Updated April 11, 2026, 1:06 p.m. ET(Update: Follow along with the latest from the 2026 Masters with our live leaderboard.)The Masters rarely disappoints when it comes to the biggest golf moments of the year. And Friday's Round 2 was no different, as Rory McIlroy had a back-nine to remember.The 2025 Masters champ shook off his bogey on No. 10 with six birdies on the final seven holes to reach 12 under for the tournament. His six-shot lead after 36 holes is the largest in the tournament's 90-year history.The question now: can McIlroy become just the fourth man to win consecutive Green Jackets, joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods?Watch the Masters live on Fubo (free trial)Here's everything you need to know about Round 3 of the Masters, including TV schedule and streaming information:What channel is the Masters on today? Time, TV scheduleAll times Eastern:Saturday, April 11: Paramount+ (noon-2 p.m.) | CBS (2-7 p.m.)Sunday, April 12: Paramount+ (noon-2 p.m.) | CBS (2-7 p.m.)Coverage of rounds 3 and 4 of the 2026 Masters will start on Paramount+, CBS' subscription streaming service, at noon before switching to CBS at 2 p.m. April 11-12. The CBS broadcast can be streamed via Fubo, which includes a free trial for new subscribers.➤ 2026 Masters purse:See record payout, breakdown by player, winner's shareWhere to watch Masters 2026 on streamingAll times Eastern:Saturday, April 11: ESPN app (10:15 a.m.-7:30 p.m.) | Masters.com and the Masters appSunday, April 12: ESPN app (10:15 a.m.-7:30 p.m.) | Masters.com and the Masters appFeatured group and hole streaming is available on PGA Tour Live on ESPN+ (available on the ESPN app with the Select plan). The main broadcast can be streamed via Fubo, which carries CBS and includes a free trial for new subscribers.Masters tee times todayRory McIlroy tees off with Sam Burns at 2:50 p.m. ET. Look through all of the Round 3 tee times.Masters location: Where is Augusta National?The Masters is the only one of golf's majors that doesn't change location each year, taking place annually at Augusta National Golf Club. Augusta, Georgia is right along the South Carolina border about 95 miles southeast of the University of Georgia in Athens and 75 miles southwest of the University of South Carolina in Columbia.Who won the Masters 2025?Rory McIlroy defeated Justin Rose on the first hole of a sudden-death playoff to win his first green jacket at the 2025 Masters, giving the 35-year-old the career grand slam. McIlroy and Rose both shot 11 under for the tournament, two shots ahead of Patrick Reed and three ahead of defending champion Scottie Scheffler.Our editors independently choose our recommendations.
